===== _commentary/v16/prompts/map3/surah_map.md (adapted) =====
Read the surah as one text and write its map of image chains: the lexical images that run through several of
its ayat and join them into one scene, process or movement. A later writer will read one ayah at a time, with
only that ayah's own dictionary. The map lets that writer hear what the ayah's words carry in the surah as a
whole, including senses whose evidence sits under the words of other ayat.

Your evidence is the surah text, the dictionary of every root in the surah (each branch with the classical
dictionaries' own phrases), an earlier reader's channel review (channels.md),
and your own knowledge of Arabic and the Quran. Where a member or passage comes from memory rather than from
the dictionary or the text, say so. Do not delegate, browse or inspect files; run only the command the header describes.

The channel review is an earlier reader's proposal. Ignore its judgements: grades,
strength or confidence labels, reading types, words such as "surprising", "exploratory" or "latent", and every
statement of what a reading may or may not do. Make your own judgement from the surah's words, the dictionary
phrases and the Quran. Do not rediscover what it already assembled: start from its chains, test each one
against the dictionary phrases and the text, and join, extend, split or correct them. Where its wording
abstracts a member, go back to the dictionary phrase and name what it actually says.

A chain belongs on the map when its members are senses the dictionary attests for words that stand in the surah,
and together they make one image or process that the surah's wording or sequence lets a listener hear. A member
need not be the sense that translates its word in its own ayah; a chain is heard across the surah, not in one
word. A chain may join a sense and its reversal as well as the parts of one scene. Mark a member attested only
inside a fixed expression [fixed expression]; add no other label to a member or a chain, and where a source
records a phrase and rejects it, say so of that phrase alone. When the dictionary itself joins two of the
surah's words in one phrase, quote that phrase: it is the strongest evidence a chain can have. Keep a scene at
the level of its objects, their parts and their operation. When proposals share members, do not fold one into
another's more abstract function unless nothing concrete is lost. Carry every chain that meets this test,
however unusual; leave out proposals that do not.

Write the map in English, with Arabic quoted exactly (surah wording from the text, dictionary phrases from the
dictionary). It is working material for the writer, not commentary prose.

1. `## Chains`. For each chain, a `###` heading naming the image. One paragraph on what the image is and how it
   moves through the surah. Then its members, one line each: the ayah ref, the word as it stands in the text,
   the root and branch id, the dictionary's own phrase quoted exactly, and what this member contributes to the
   image. Add Quran passages outside the surah, with exact refs, where they stage or confirm the chain; for
   each, name the speaker and the situation in a few words, and include the ayah that opens its scene when the
   passage continues one.
2. `## Interactions`. Where chains meet: a shared member, a dictionary phrase that joins members of two chains,
   a Quran passage that stages two chains together, or one chain's scene needing another's. One line each: the
   chains, where they meet, the evidence.
3. `## Ayat`. For each ayah in order: the chains its words take part in, what its words add to each, and in one
   line the whole scene each chain makes across the surah, so that a writer who sees only this ayah sees the
   scene, not a fragment.
4. `## Not carried`. Each channel subchannel you did not carry into a chain: one short line
   each, its name and why, no prose.

No ranking and no labels of strength or confidence. No list of what a writer must include. There is no length
target and no required number of chains or members.

===== _commentary/v16/work/s023/surah.r2/text.md =====
# Surah 23

- 23:1 قَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ
- 23:2 ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ فِى صَلَاتِهِمْ خَٰشِعُونَ
- 23:3 وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنِ ٱللَّغْوِ مُعْرِضُونَ
- 23:4 وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِلزَّكَوٰةِ فَٰعِلُونَ
- 23:5 وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَٰفِظُونَ
- 23:6 إِلَّا عَلَىٰٓ أَزْوَٰجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ
- 23:7 فَمَنِ ٱبْتَغَىٰ وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْعَادُونَ
- 23:8 وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَٰنَٰتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَٰعُونَ
- 23:9 وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلَوَٰتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ
- 23:10 أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْوَٰرِثُونَ
- 23:11 ٱلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ ٱلْفِرْدَوْسَ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
- 23:12 وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ مِن سُلَٰلَةٍۢ مِّن طِينٍۢ
- 23:13 ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَٰهُ نُطْفَةًۭ فِى قَرَارٍۢ مَّكِينٍۢ
- 23:14 ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا ٱلنُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةًۭ فَخَلَقْنَا ٱلْعَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةًۭ فَخَلَقْنَا ٱلْمُضْغَةَ عِظَٰمًۭا فَكَسَوْنَا ٱلْعِظَٰمَ لَحْمًۭا ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَٰهُ خَلْقًا ءَاخَرَ ۚ فَتَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ ٱلْخَٰلِقِينَ
- 23:15 ثُمَّ إِنَّكُم بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ لَمَيِّتُونَ
- 23:16 ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ تُبْعَثُونَ
- 23:17 وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعَ طَرَآئِقَ وَمَا كُنَّا عَنِ ٱلْخَلْقِ غَٰفِلِينَ
- 23:18 وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۢ بِقَدَرٍۢ فَأَسْكَنَّٰهُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۖ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰ ذَهَابٍۭ بِهِۦ لَقَٰدِرُونَ
- 23:19 فَأَنشَأْنَا لَكُم بِهِۦ جَنَّٰتٍۢ مِّن نَّخِيلٍۢ وَأَعْنَٰبٍۢ لَّكُمْ فِيهَا فَوَٰكِهُ كَثِيرَةٌۭ وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ
- 23:20 وَشَجَرَةًۭ تَخْرُجُ مِن طُورِ سَيْنَآءَ تَنۢبُتُ بِٱلدُّهْنِ وَصِبْغٍۢ لِّلْءَاكِلِينَ
- 23:21 وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ لَعِبْرَةًۭ ۖ نُّسْقِيكُم مِّمَّا فِى بُطُونِهَا وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَٰفِعُ كَثِيرَةٌۭ وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ
- 23:22 وَعَلَيْهَا وَعَلَى ٱلْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ
- 23:23 وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ فَقَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥٓ ۖ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
- 23:24 فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌۭ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتَفَضَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَنزَلَ مَلَٰٓئِكَةًۭ مَّا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِىٓ ءَابَآئِنَا ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
- 23:25 إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلٌۢ بِهِۦ جِنَّةٌۭ فَتَرَبَّصُوا۟ بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍۢ
- 23:26 قَالَ رَبِّ ٱنصُرْنِى بِمَا كَذَّبُونِ
- 23:27 فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ ۙ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّۢ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ ۖ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ ۖ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ
- 23:28 فَإِذَا ٱسْتَوَيْتَ أَنتَ وَمَن مَّعَكَ عَلَى ٱلْفُلْكِ فَقُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى نَجَّىٰنَا مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
- 23:29 وَقُل رَّبِّ أَنزِلْنِى مُنزَلًۭا مُّبَارَكًۭا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْمُنزِلِينَ
- 23:30 إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ وَإِن كُنَّا لَمُبْتَلِينَ
- 23:31 ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَا مِنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ قَرْنًا ءَاخَرِينَ
- 23:32 فَأَرْسَلْنَا فِيهِمْ رَسُولًۭا مِّنْهُمْ أَنِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥٓ ۖ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
- 23:33 وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ مِن قَوْمِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَكَذَّبُوا۟ بِلِقَآءِ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ وَأَتْرَفْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌۭ مِّثْلُكُمْ يَأْكُلُ مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ مِنْهُ وَيَشْرَبُ مِمَّا تَشْرَبُونَ
- 23:34 وَلَئِنْ أَطَعْتُم بَشَرًۭا مِّثْلَكُمْ إِنَّكُمْ إِذًۭا لَّخَٰسِرُونَ
- 23:35 أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَابًۭا وَعِظَٰمًا أَنَّكُم مُّخْرَجُونَ
- 23:36 ۞ هَيْهَاتَ هَيْهَاتَ لِمَا تُوعَدُونَ
- 23:37 إِنْ هِىَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا ٱلدُّنْيَا نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيَا وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَبْعُوثِينَ
- 23:38 إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلٌ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًۭا وَمَا نَحْنُ لَهُۥ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ
- 23:39 قَالَ رَبِّ ٱنصُرْنِى بِمَا كَذَّبُونِ
- 23:40 قَالَ عَمَّا قَلِيلٍۢ لَّيُصْبِحُنَّ نَٰدِمِينَ
- 23:41 فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلصَّيْحَةُ بِٱلْحَقِّ فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ غُثَآءًۭ ۚ فَبُعْدًۭا لِّلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
- 23:42 ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَا مِنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ قُرُونًا ءَاخَرِينَ
- 23:43 مَا تَسْبِقُ مِنْ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلَهَا وَمَا يَسْتَـْٔخِرُونَ
- 23:44 ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلَنَا تَتْرَا ۖ كُلَّ مَا جَآءَ أُمَّةًۭ رَّسُولُهَا كَذَّبُوهُ ۚ فَأَتْبَعْنَا بَعْضَهُم بَعْضًۭا وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ أَحَادِيثَ ۚ فَبُعْدًۭا لِّقَوْمٍۢ لَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ
- 23:45 ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَأَخَاهُ هَٰرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَسُلْطَٰنٍۢ مُّبِينٍ
- 23:46 إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَإِي۟هِۦ فَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا عَالِينَ
- 23:47 فَقَالُوٓا۟ أَنُؤْمِنُ لِبَشَرَيْنِ مِثْلِنَا وَقَوْمُهُمَا لَنَا عَٰبِدُونَ
- 23:48 فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَكَانُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلْمُهْلَكِينَ
- 23:49 وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَٰبَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ
- 23:50 وَجَعَلْنَا ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُۥٓ ءَايَةًۭ وَءَاوَيْنَٰهُمَآ إِلَىٰ رَبْوَةٍۢ ذَاتِ قَرَارٍۢ وَمَعِينٍۢ
- 23:51 يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلرُّسُلُ كُلُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَٱعْمَلُوا۟ صَٰلِحًا ۖ إِنِّى بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِيمٌۭ
- 23:52 وَإِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ وَأَنَا۠ رَبُّكُمْ فَٱتَّقُونِ
- 23:53 فَتَقَطَّعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ زُبُرًۭا ۖ كُلُّ حِزْبٍۭ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ
- 23:54 فَذَرْهُمْ فِى غَمْرَتِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ
- 23:55 أَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّمَا نُمِدُّهُم بِهِۦ مِن مَّالٍۢ وَبَنِينَ
- 23:56 نُسَارِعُ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ ۚ بَل لَّا يَشْعُرُونَ
- 23:57 إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ هُم مِّنْ خَشْيَةِ رَبِّهِم مُّشْفِقُونَ
- 23:58 وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ
- 23:59 وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِرَبِّهِمْ لَا يُشْرِكُونَ
- 23:60 وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ مَآ ءَاتَوا۟ وَّقُلُوبُهُمْ وَجِلَةٌ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ رَٰجِعُونَ
- 23:61 أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَهُمْ لَهَا سَٰبِقُونَ
- 23:62 وَلَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا ۖ وَلَدَيْنَا كِتَٰبٌۭ يَنطِقُ بِٱلْحَقِّ ۚ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ
- 23:63 بَلْ قُلُوبُهُمْ فِى غَمْرَةٍۢ مِّنْ هَٰذَا وَلَهُمْ أَعْمَٰلٌۭ مِّن دُونِ ذَٰلِكَ هُمْ لَهَا عَٰمِلُونَ
- 23:64 حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَخَذْنَا مُتْرَفِيهِم بِٱلْعَذَابِ إِذَا هُمْ يَجْـَٔرُونَ
- 23:65 لَا تَجْـَٔرُوا۟ ٱلْيَوْمَ ۖ إِنَّكُم مِّنَّا لَا تُنصَرُونَ
- 23:66 قَدْ كَانَتْ ءَايَٰتِى تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ فَكُنتُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْقَٰبِكُمْ تَنكِصُونَ
- 23:67 مُسْتَكْبِرِينَ بِهِۦ سَٰمِرًۭا تَهْجُرُونَ
- 23:68 أَفَلَمْ يَدَّبَّرُوا۟ ٱلْقَوْلَ أَمْ جَآءَهُم مَّا لَمْ يَأْتِ ءَابَآءَهُمُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
- 23:69 أَمْ لَمْ يَعْرِفُوا۟ رَسُولَهُمْ فَهُمْ لَهُۥ مُنكِرُونَ
- 23:70 أَمْ يَقُولُونَ بِهِۦ جِنَّةٌۢ ۚ بَلْ جَآءَهُم بِٱلْحَقِّ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ لِلْحَقِّ كَٰرِهُونَ
- 23:71 وَلَوِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْحَقُّ أَهْوَآءَهُمْ لَفَسَدَتِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ وَمَن فِيهِنَّ ۚ بَلْ أَتَيْنَٰهُم بِذِكْرِهِمْ فَهُمْ عَن ذِكْرِهِم مُّعْرِضُونَ
- 23:72 أَمْ تَسْـَٔلُهُمْ خَرْجًۭا فَخَرَاجُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌۭ ۖ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ
- 23:73 وَإِنَّكَ لَتَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍۢ مُّسْتَقِيمٍۢ
- 23:74 وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ عَنِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ لَنَٰكِبُونَ
- 23:75 ۞ وَلَوْ رَحِمْنَٰهُمْ وَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِم مِّن ضُرٍّۢ لَّلَجُّوا۟ فِى طُغْيَٰنِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ
- 23:76 وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْنَٰهُم بِٱلْعَذَابِ فَمَا ٱسْتَكَانُوا۟ لِرَبِّهِمْ وَمَا يَتَضَرَّعُونَ
- 23:77 حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِم بَابًۭا ذَا عَذَابٍۢ شَدِيدٍ إِذَا هُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ
- 23:78 وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ وَٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةَ ۚ قَلِيلًۭا مَّا تَشْكُرُونَ
- 23:79 وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى ذَرَأَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَإِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ
- 23:80 وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُحْىِۦ وَيُمِيتُ وَلَهُ ٱخْتِلَٰفُ ٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
- 23:81 بَلْ قَالُوا۟ مِثْلَ مَا قَالَ ٱلْأَوَّلُونَ
- 23:82 قَالُوٓا۟ أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًۭا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ
- 23:83 لَقَدْ وُعِدْنَا نَحْنُ وَءَابَآؤُنَا هَٰذَا مِن قَبْلُ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
- 23:84 قُل لِّمَنِ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَمَن فِيهَآ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
- 23:85 سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ ۚ قُلْ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
- 23:86 قُلْ مَن رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ ٱلسَّبْعِ وَرَبُّ ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
- 23:87 سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ ۚ قُلْ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
- 23:88 قُلْ مَنۢ بِيَدِهِۦ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ وَهُوَ يُجِيرُ وَلَا يُجَارُ عَلَيْهِ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
- 23:89 سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ ۚ قُلْ فَأَنَّىٰ تُسْحَرُونَ
- 23:90 بَلْ أَتَيْنَٰهُم بِٱلْحَقِّ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
- 23:91 مَا ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِن وَلَدٍۢ وَمَا كَانَ مَعَهُۥ مِنْ إِلَٰهٍ ۚ إِذًۭا لَّذَهَبَ كُلُّ إِلَٰهٍۭ بِمَا خَلَقَ وَلَعَلَا بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ ۚ سُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
- 23:92 عَٰلِمِ ٱلْغَيْبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ فَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
- 23:93 قُل رَّبِّ إِمَّا تُرِيَنِّى مَا يُوعَدُونَ
- 23:94 رَبِّ فَلَا تَجْعَلْنِى فِى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
- 23:95 وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّرِيَكَ مَا نَعِدُهُمْ لَقَٰدِرُونَ
- 23:96 ٱدْفَعْ بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ ٱلسَّيِّئَةَ ۚ نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَصِفُونَ
- 23:97 وَقُل رَّبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ هَمَزَٰتِ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينِ
- 23:98 وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ رَبِّ أَن يَحْضُرُونِ
- 23:99 حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَهُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ قَالَ رَبِّ ٱرْجِعُونِ
- 23:100 لَعَلِّىٓ أَعْمَلُ صَٰلِحًۭا فِيمَا تَرَكْتُ ۚ كَلَّآ ۚ إِنَّهَا كَلِمَةٌ هُوَ قَآئِلُهَا ۖ وَمِن وَرَآئِهِم بَرْزَخٌ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
- 23:101 فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَلَآ أَنسَابَ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ وَلَا يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
- 23:102 فَمَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ
- 23:103 وَمَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ فِى جَهَنَّمَ خَٰلِدُونَ
- 23:104 تَلْفَحُ وُجُوهَهُمُ ٱلنَّارُ وَهُمْ فِيهَا كَٰلِحُونَ
- 23:105 أَلَمْ تَكُنْ ءَايَٰتِى تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ فَكُنتُم بِهَا تُكَذِّبُونَ
- 23:106 قَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَا غَلَبَتْ عَلَيْنَا شِقْوَتُنَا وَكُنَّا قَوْمًۭا ضَآلِّينَ
- 23:107 رَبَّنَآ أَخْرِجْنَا مِنْهَا فَإِنْ عُدْنَا فَإِنَّا ظَٰلِمُونَ
- 23:108 قَالَ ٱخْسَـُٔوا۟ فِيهَا وَلَا تُكَلِّمُونِ
- 23:109 إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ فَرِيقٌۭ مِّنْ عِبَادِى يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ ءَامَنَّا فَٱغْفِرْ لَنَا وَٱرْحَمْنَا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
- 23:110 فَٱتَّخَذْتُمُوهُمْ سِخْرِيًّا حَتَّىٰٓ أَنسَوْكُمْ ذِكْرِى وَكُنتُم مِّنْهُمْ تَضْحَكُونَ
- 23:111 إِنِّى جَزَيْتُهُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ بِمَا صَبَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّهُمْ هُمُ ٱلْفَآئِزُونَ
- 23:112 قَٰلَ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ عَدَدَ سِنِينَ
- 23:113 قَالُوا۟ لَبِثْنَا يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍۢ فَسْـَٔلِ ٱلْعَآدِّينَ
- 23:114 قَٰلَ إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا ۖ لَّوْ أَنَّكُمْ كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
- 23:115 أَفَحَسِبْتُمْ أَنَّمَا خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ عَبَثًۭا وَأَنَّكُمْ إِلَيْنَا لَا تُرْجَعُونَ
- 23:116 فَتَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱلْحَقُّ ۖ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱلْكَرِيمِ
- 23:117 وَمَن يَدْعُ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ لَا بُرْهَٰنَ لَهُۥ بِهِۦ فَإِنَّمَا حِسَابُهُۥ عِندَ رَبِّهِۦٓ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ
- 23:118 وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱغْفِرْ وَٱرْحَمْ وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ

# Dictionary: every branch of every focus root

Every root of the surah's words, each once, headed by the ayah and word where it first occurs; it also serves the later words listed with it.
One entry per branch: a Turkish label and Turkish glosses of its attested senses, then the classical dictionaries' own phrases with their source tags (ayn, sihah, tahdhib, maqayis, mufradat, jamhara). [kalıp] marks a sense the dictionaries attest only inside a fixed expression.
Identity roots come from the quran-data gateway. Word-scoped alternatives are cited analyses of this
exact word. **Echo roots** are observed but withheld mappings: sound-family candidates, not identity.

## ف ل ح (root_001175): 23:1 أَفْلَحَ, 23:102 ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ, 23:117 يُفْلِحُ

  أصل يدل على شق (maqayis)؛ فلحت الأرض شققتها (maqayis;sihah;tahdhib)؛ فلحت الشيء إذا شققته أو قطعته (jamhara)؛ الحديد بالحديد يفلح أي يشق أو يقطع (maqayis;ayn;jamhara;sihah;tahdhib;mufradat)

  الفلح الشق في الشفة (ayn;tahdhib)؛ الأفلح المشقوق الشفة السفلى (maqayis;jamhara;sihah;tahdhib)؛ امرأة فلحاء وعنترة الفلحاء لفلحة كانت به (maqayis;jamhara;sihah;tahdhib)

- **B004** çiftçiye benzetilen ücretli taşıyıcı — çiftçiye benzetilerek adlandırılan ücretli taşıyıcı
  الفلاح المكاري وإنما قيل له فلاح تشبيها بالأكار (ayn;tahdhib)؛ وجعله ابن أحمر المكاري (jamhara)

  الأصل الثاني الفلاح البقاء والفوز (maqayis)؛ الفلاح والفلح البقاء في الخير (ayn;tahdhib)؛ الفلح والفلاح البقاء (jamhara)؛ الفلاح الفوز والنجاة والبقاء (sihah)؛ أفلح وأنجح إذا أدرك مطلوبه (jamhara)؛ استفلحي بأمرك أي فوزي أو اظفري بأمرك (maqayis;sihah;tahdhib)؛ الفلاح الظفر وإدراك بغية (mufradat)
- **B006** orucu sürdürmeye güç veren şafak öncesi öğün — şafak öncesi öğün · şafak öncesi öğünü ya da gece ibadetinin kazancını kaçırmaktan korkmak
  الفلاح السحور (maqayis;ayn;sihah;tahdhib)؛ سمي فلاحا لأن الإنسان تبقى معه قوته على الصوم (maqayis)؛ لأن به بقاء الصوم (sihah;tahdhib)؛ سمي السحور الفلاح (mufradat)
- **B007** alışverişi çekici gösterme; yalanla kandırma ve alaya alma — satış ve alışverişi satıcıya ve alıcıya çekici göstermek · satış ve alışverişi satıcıya ve alıcıya çekici göstermek · onları kandırıp gerçeğe aykırı söz söylemek · başkasını daha yüksek bedel vermeye kandırmak için kiracının bedeli artırması · kandırma ve alaya alma
  فلحت للقوم وبالقوم أفلح فلاحة وهو أن يزين البيع والشراء للبائع والمشتري (tahdhib)؛ فلحت بهم تفليحا إذا مكر بهم وقال لهم غير الحق (tahdhib)؛ الفلح النجس وهو زيادة المكتري ليزيد غيره فيغر به (tahdhib)؛ التفليح المكر والاستهزاء (tahdhib)

## ء م ن (root_000054): 23:1 ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ, 23:8 لِأَمَٰنَٰتِهِمْ, 23:38 بِمُؤْمِنِينَ, 23:44 يُؤْمِنُونَ, 23:47 أَنُؤْمِنُ, 23:58 يُؤْمِنُونَ, 23:74 يُؤْمِنُونَ, 23:109 ءَامَنَّا

# s023 Semantic Channel Discovery

## Parent Channels

### 1. P1: Custody as Bounded Continuity
- Semantic invariant: What is entrusted endures when access, movement, and succession are kept within a watched boundary.
- Surface relation: direct; 23:5-11 moves from guarding bodily openings and covenants to inheritance and lasting residence.
- Surprising reach: Ethical fidelity materializes as frontier defense, pastoral governance, road control, and the preservation of a tenancy across succession.

#### Subchannel A. Covenant Watch
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A custodian receives an entrusted charge, watches it continuously, and preserves its covenantal limits.
- Active motifs: secure trust `quranic:root_000054:B001/m01`; custodial guarding `quranic:root_000342:B001/m01`; protected sanctuary `quranic:root_000342:B006/m01`; preserved covenant `quranic:root_000342:B006/m02`; shepherd-governor `quranic:root_000574:B002/m01`; covenant preservation `quranic:root_000574:B006/m01`; repeated care `quranic:root_001055:B001/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:5 حَٰفِظُونَ; 23:8 أَمَٰنَٰتِ / عَهْدِ / رَٰعُونَ; 23:9 يُحَافِظُ.
- Synthesis: Trust is not a passive possession. The branch images stage it as a charge under custody: a shepherd governs what is within the enclosure, repeated care keeps it sound, and the same guarding operation protects sanctuary, chastity, and covenant.

#### Subchannel B. Bodily Frontier and Controlled Passage
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Openings and routes are protected against movement that crosses the authorized frontier.
- Active motifs: fissure opening `quranic:root_001139:B001/m01`; exposed frontier `quranic:root_001139:B004/m01`; transgression beyond a limit `quranic:root_000993:B001/m01`; the far side of a barrier `quranic:root_001642:B006/m01`; overreaching aggression `quranic:root_000138:B003/m01`; clear guarded road `quranic:root_000342:B007/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:5 فُرُوجِ / حَٰفِظُونَ; 23:7 ٱبْتَغَىٰ / وَرَآءَ / عَادُونَ.
- Synthesis: The bodily opening becomes a frontier and the prohibited act becomes unauthorized passage. Seeking “beyond” is thereby reframed as crossing onto the wrong side of a guarded route, not merely choosing an abstract moral alternative.

#### Subchannel C. Durable Tenancy and Succession
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A protected estate passes to successors and remains their settled possession.
- Active motifs: inherited estate `quranic:root_001639:B001/m01`; grant received without prior labor `quranic:root_001639:B002/m01`; enduring permanence `quranic:root_000429:B001/m01`; clinging residence `quranic:root_000429:B002/m01`; covenant preservation `quranic:root_000574:B006/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:8 رَٰعُونَ; 23:10 وَٰرِثُونَ; 23:11 يَرِثُ / خَٰلِدُونَ.
- Synthesis: Inheritance completes the custody scene. What was guarded becomes a durable tenancy, and permanence is rendered as remaining attached to an inherited place rather than as duration alone.

### 2. P1: Staged Embodiment
- Semantic invariant: A body comes into being through measured extraction, adhesion, component formation, and covering.
- Surface relation: direct; 23:12-14 explicitly presents successive material transformations.
- Surprising reach: Embryogenesis is also a workshop and textile process in which measured stock is drawn out, fixed in a container, joined, and clothed.

#### Subchannel A. Extraction and Material Forming
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Raw material is measured, drawn from a source, and prepared for fabrication.
- Active motifs: measurement before forming `quranic:root_000434:B001/m01`; cutting to measured form `quranic:root_000434:B001/m02`; originating a created object `quranic:root_000434:B002/m01`; gentle extraction `quranic:root_000736:B001/m01`; clay stock `quranic:root_000963:B001/m01`; fine workmanship in clay `quranic:root_000963:B005/m01`; generative clear fluid `quranic:root_001518:B002/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:12 خَلَقْ / سُلَٰلَةٍ / طِينٍ; 23:13 نُطْفَةً; 23:14 خَلَقْ / نُّطْفَةَ.
- Synthesis: Creation begins as an exacting material operation. The source is gently drawn out, clay supplies workable stock, and “creating” retains the latent force of measuring and cutting a form to specification.

#### Subchannel B. Implantation and Adhesive Transformation
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Fluid is implanted in a stable receptacle, adheres, thickens, and becomes a worked lump.
- Active motifs: generative fluid settled in the womb `quranic:root_001215:B013/m01`; adhesion to a support `quranic:root_001039:B001/m01`; clotted blood `quranic:root_001039:B003/m01`; blood-sucking leech `quranic:root_001039:B003/m02`; implanted pregnancy `quranic:root_001039:B009/m01`; chewed embryonic lump `quranic:root_001429:B002/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:13 قَرَارٍ; 23:14 عَلَقَةً / مُضْغَةً.
- Synthesis: The stable “place” acts as a receptacle rather than a neutral location. Within it, attachment is the operative hinge: suspension becomes clotting, then a malleable lump whose shape bears the trace of working.

#### Subchannel C. Skeletal Clothing and Joined Flesh
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A rigid frame is assembled, covered, and joined into an integrated body.
- Active motifs: bone structure `quranic:root_001029:B005/m01`; clothing a body `quranic:root_001300:B001/m01`; covering bone with flesh `quranic:root_001300:B002/m01`; bodily flesh `quranic:root_001348:B002/m01`; soldered adhesion `quranic:root_001348:B005/m01`; textile weft `quranic:root_001348:B006/m01`; originating creation `quranic:root_001502:B006/m01`; rearing development `quranic:root_001502:B006/m02`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:14 عِظَٰمًا / كَسَوْ / لَحْمًا / أَنشَأْ.
- Synthesis: Flesh is simultaneously body material, joining medium, and textile weft. The skeleton is therefore not merely covered; it is clothed and soldered into a coherent fabric before the new creature is raised.

### 3. P1: Measured Water Becomes Yield
- Semantic invariant: Water is apportioned, settled, routed, and converted into cultivated output.
- Surface relation: direct; 23:17-21 follows measured rain into earth, gardens, crops, oil, drink, and food.
- Surprising reach: Cosmic provision takes the form of hydraulic administration and agricultural processing rather than undifferentiated abundance.

#### Subchannel A. Descent, Storage, and Withdrawal
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Water descends from an elevated source, arrives in a measured allotment, settles in storage, and remains withdrawable.
- Active motifs: descent from above `quranic:root_001492:B001/m01`; settlement in a place `quranic:root_001492:B001/m02`; overhead sky as rain source `quranic:root_000745:B004/m01`; water as stored substance `quranic:root_001458:B001/m01`; abundant water inrush `quranic:root_001458:B002/m01`; measured quantity `quranic:root_001205:B001/m01`; apportioned design `quranic:root_001205:B005/m01`; stable dwelling `quranic:root_000726:B002/m01`; removal along a course `quranic:root_000522:B006/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:17 سَّمَآءِ; 23:18 أَنزَلْ / مَآءً / قَدَرٍ / أَسْكَ / ذَهَابٍ.
- Synthesis: The rainfall is a managed transfer. It is designed in advance, metered, housed in the ground, and held under the same capacity that could send it away, making availability depend on controlled storage rather than chance.

#### Subchannel B. Irrigation and Cultivated Emergence
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Stored water is made available through channels and converted into planted growth and crop yield.
- Active motifs: giving drink `quranic:root_000722:B001/m01`; making water available by canal `quranic:root_000722:B002/m01`; irrigation share `quranic:root_000722:B003/m01`; plant emergence `quranic:root_001465:B001/m01`; deliberate cultivation `quranic:root_001465:B002/m01`; enclosed garden `quranic:root_000266:B003/m01`; crop yield `quranic:root_000043:B002/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:19 جَنَّٰتٍ / تَأْكُلُ; 23:20 تَنۢبُتُ; 23:21 نُّسْقِي / تَأْكُلُ.
- Synthesis: Water moves from storage into a distribution system. Canal, share, cultivation, enclosed garden, and edible yield form one production chain in which provision is materialized as managed irrigation.

#### Subchannel C. Orchard Processing
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Trees and fruit are selected as raw produce, then expressed as oil, dye, condiment, and food.
- Active motifs: date-palm crop `quranic:root_001483:B001/m01`; grapes `quranic:root_001050:B001/m01`; tree stock `quranic:root_000777:B001/m01`; oil material `quranic:root_000497:B001/m01`; coating action `quranic:root_000497:B001/m02`; dyeing `quranic:root_000842:B001/m01`; condiment `quranic:root_000842:B002/m01`; consumption `quranic:root_000043:B001/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:19 نَّخِيلٍ / أَعْنَٰبٍ / تَأْكُلُ; 23:20 شَجَرَةً / دُّهْنِ / صِبْغٍ / ءَاكِلِينَ.
- Synthesis: The orchard is not only a field of growth. Its output enters a compact processing scene: tree and fruit become oil that coats, pigment that transforms a surface, condiment that accompanies food, and finally nourishment.

### 4. P1: Carriers Across Contained Media
- Semantic invariant: Sustenance and passengers move because a containing body bears them through a medium.
- Surface relation: direct; 23:21-22 joins livestock interiors, human benefit, carrying animals, and ships.
- Surprising reach: Animal body, howdah, hull, and rudder become analogous transport containers.

#### Subchannel A. Livestock as Interior Provision and Load-Bearer
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A living carrier contains drink, yields benefit, and bears external loads.
- Active motifs: livestock herd `quranic:root_001525:B005/m01`; animal interior `quranic:root_000128:B001/m01`; abdominal fluid `quranic:root_000722:B005/m01`; usable benefit `quranic:root_001536:B001/m01`; carrying a load `quranic:root_000357:B001/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:21 أَنْعَٰمِ / بُطُونِ / نُّسْقِي / مَنَٰفِعُ; 23:22 تُحْمَلُ.
- Synthesis: The animal is both container and vehicle. Its interior supplies drink, its body provides multiple uses, and the same embodied capacity extends outward into carrying.

#### Subchannel B. Hull, Rudder, and Crossing
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A vessel carries its occupants while a steering component stabilizes passage through disturbed water.
- Active motifs: ship `quranic:root_001177:B003/m01`; turbulent wave `quranic:root_001177:B007/m01`; carrying body `quranic:root_000357:B001/m01`; howdah-like carrier `quranic:root_000357:B006/m01`; ship rudder `quranic:root_000726:B008/m01`; crossing from one side to another `quranic:root_000974:B001/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:18 أَسْكَ; 23:21 عِبْرَةً; 23:22 فُلْكِ / تُحْمَلُ.
- Synthesis: The sparse transport image resolves into a small naval mechanism: the hull bears, the wave supplies resistance, and the rudder arrests uncontrolled motion so that crossing can occur.

### 5. P2: Vessel Construction Under Oversight
- Semantic invariant: Rescue is prepared through supervised fabrication, ordered loading, stabilization, and correct landing.
- Surface relation: direct; 23:27-30 gives construction, loading, embarkation, deliverance, and landing instructions.
- Surprising reach: Revelation functions like a build specification and loading manifest, while divine sight becomes workshop inspection.

#### Subchannel A. Supervised Fabrication
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Skilled makers construct a vessel under continuous inspection and an inscribed specification.
- Active motifs: making an object `quranic:root_000885:B001/m01`; skilled handcraft `quranic:root_000885:B002/m01`; constructed water basin `quranic:root_000885:B006/m01`; supervisory eye `quranic:root_001069:B003/m01`; choice quality `quranic:root_001069:B014/m01`; inscribed specification `quranic:root_001633:B003/m01`; divine specification `quranic:root_001633:B004/m01`; ship `quranic:root_001177:B003/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:27 ٱصْنَعِ / فُلْكَ / أَعْيُنِ / أَوْحَيْ / وَحْيِ.
- Synthesis: The vessel is a fabricated work whose construction is watched and specified. The eye supplies inspection, revelation supplies the design communication, and the “manufactories” sense adds the built basin or works-yard around the craft.

#### Subchannel B. Loading by Pair and Manifest
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Cargo is inserted according to an ordered pairing rule, with prior status determining inclusion.
- Active motifs: insertion through a channel `quranic:root_000735:B002/m01`; sewing thread through material `quranic:root_000735:B004/m01`; paired counterparts `quranic:root_000652:B001/m01`; active pairing `quranic:root_000652:B003/m01`; joining one to one as two `quranic:root_000208:B001/m01`; ordered precedence `quranic:root_000671:B001/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:27 ٱسْلُكْ / زَوْجَيْنِ / ٱثْنَيْنِ / سَبَقَ.
- Synthesis: Loading is rendered as threading selected units into the hull. Pairing is an operation, not just a count, and precedence acts as the manifest rule that distinguishes those already assigned from those admitted.

#### Subchannel C. Leveling, Escape, and Landing
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The vessel levels out, separates from danger, and alights in a stable, properly placed berth.

- Synthesis: The exchange treats earthly duration as a residence ledger. Years, days, recurring counts, and comparative smallness convert felt time into a measured interval whose scale changes when placed inside a larger duration.

#### Subchannel B. Calculation Against Purposeless Play
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Measured creation is tested against the alternative of unplanned mixing with no return destination.
- Active motifs: reckoning an account `quranic:root_000318:B001/m02`; unsupported supposition `quranic:root_000318:B002/m01`; measurement before forming `quranic:root_000434:B001/m01`; cutting to measured form `quranic:root_000434:B001/m02`; originating creation `quranic:root_000434:B002/m01`; random mixture `quranic:root_000972:B001/m01`; play without valid purpose `quranic:root_000972:B002/m01`; return to the point of origin `quranic:root_000544:B001/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:115 حَسِبْ / خَلَقْ / عَبَثًا / تُرْجَعُ.
- Synthesis: Creation is measured work, so purposelessness would be a contradiction in its production logic. Random mixture and play describe a process without specification or destination; return supplies the intended endpoint that calculation requires.

### 28. P5: Covering Mercy
- Semantic invariant: Mercy restores security by re-covering exposed fault and re-enclosing the vulnerable within protective relation.
- Surface relation: direct; 23:109 and 23:118 pair belief, forgiveness, mercy, goodness, and repeated petition.
- Surprising reach: Forgiveness behaves as protective clothing and wound care, while mercy expands into kinship and womb-like enclosure.

#### Subchannel A. Protective Covering
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Fault is covered so that its bearer is protected from the continuing effect of exposure.
- Active motifs: protective covering `quranic:root_001096:B001/m01`; protective covering of fault `quranic:root_001096:B002/m01`; hair-like surface nap `quranic:root_001096:B003/m01`; tender mercy `quranic:root_000552:B001/m01`; secure trust `quranic:root_000054:B001/m01`; heart-settled belief `quranic:root_000054:B002/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:109 ءَامَ / ٱغْفِرْ / ٱرْحَمْ; 23:118 ٱغْفِرْ / ٱرْحَمْ.
- Synthesis: Forgiveness is a surface operation with an interior outcome. A protective layer covers the exposed fault, mercy attends the bearer, and security returns to the heart.

#### Subchannel B. Kin and Womb Enclosure
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: The vulnerable person is received into a kin-like, womb-like field of care and gift.
- Active motifs: kin relation `quranic:root_000552:B002/m01`; womb `quranic:root_000552:B003/m01`; selected excellence `quranic:root_000452:B002/m01`; generous gift `quranic:root_000452:B005/m01`; wound relapse `quranic:root_001096:B004/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:109 خَيْرُ / ٱرْحَمْ / رَّٰحِمِينَ / ٱغْفِرْ; 23:118 خَيْرُ / ٱرْحَمْ / رَّٰحِمِينَ / ٱغْفِرْ.
- Synthesis: Mercy can be read as re-entry into protective relation. Kin and womb supply the enclosure, excellence supplies selection for care, gift supplies the positive grant, and the wound-relapse sense keeps restoration attentive to recurring vulnerability.

## Standalone Subchannels

### S1. P1: Noise Filtration
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Unproductive sound is identified as discard, noise, and deviation, then turned away from the active channel.
- Active motifs: matter excluded from account `quranic:root_001361:B001/m01`; clamor `quranic:root_001361:B003/m01`; veering from the right course `quranic:root_001361:B005/m01`; turning one’s side away `quranic:root_001001:B005/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:3 لَّغْوِ / مُعْرِضُونَ.
- Synthesis: The surface rejection of idle speech becomes a filtering operation. Noise is treated as material with no account, and turning away removes it from both the speech channel and the directed course.

### S2. P1: Hidden Fire Circuit
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A dormant ember is struck, fed, and transmitted as a continuing heat source.
- Active motifs: exposure to fire heat `quranic:root_000879:B001/m01`; latent fire struck from flint `quranic:root_001642:B002/m01`; feeding fire `quranic:root_000043:B005/m01`; stoking inherited embers `quranic:root_001639:B005/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:2 and 23:9 صَلَاتِ / صَلَوَٰتِ; 23:7 وَرَآءَ; 23:10-11 وَٰرِثُونَ / يَرِثُ; 23:19 and 23:21 تَأْكُلُ.
- Synthesis: Prayer, what lies beyond, inheritance, and eating activate a complete fire scene: latent heat is struck, fuel is consumed, and embers are kept alive across succession.

### S3. P2: Speculative Waiting Market
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Goods are withheld while traders wait for a chosen time to act.
- Active motifs: watchful waiting `quranic:root_000534:B001/m01`; holding merchandise in expectation `quranic:root_000534:B002/m01`; appointed time `quranic:root_000382:B001/m01`; setting a time for action `quranic:root_000382:B003/m01`; waiting for the moment `quranic:root_000382:B005/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:25 تَرَبَّصُ / حِينٍ.
- Synthesis: “Wait for him” opens a compact market frame. The object is held like merchandise while participants speculate on timing, making delay an interested economic action rather than neutral patience.

### S4. P2: Raid Cry and Full-Draw Bow
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: An alarm cry initiates a competitive shot from a fully drawn and tensioned bow.
- Active motifs: full bow draw `quranic:root_001080:B004/m01`; bowstring `quranic:root_001621:B007/m01`; wagered competition `quranic:root_000671:B002/m01`; loud cry `quranic:root_000895:B001/m01`; terrifying alarm `quranic:root_000895:B002/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:27 سَبَقَ / مُّغْرَقُونَ; 23:41 صَّيْحَةُ; 23:43 تَسْبِقُ; 23:44 تَتْرَا.
- Synthesis: The construction paths complete an armed launch scene: the bow reaches full draw, its string stores force, competition fixes the target relation, and the cry marks release or raid onset.

### S5. P3: Elevated Refuge and Spring
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Vulnerable persons are gathered onto high stable ground supplied by visible flowing water.
- Active motifs: gathering into a place of refuge `quranic:root_000070:B001/m01`; compassionate shelter `quranic:root_000070:B002/m01`; elevated ground `quranic:root_000537:B002/m01`; upward rise `quranic:root_000537:B001/m01`; stable settlement `quranic:root_001215:B003/m01`; spring `quranic:root_001069:B006/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:50 ءَاوَيْ / رَبْوَةٍ / قَرَارٍ / مَعِينٍ.
- Synthesis: Refuge is topographic and hydraulic. Safety requires both elevation above threat and a stable spring-fed settlement, joining protection, rise, fixity, and water in one compact scene.

### S6. P3: Proof as Sharp Instrument
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Authority advances with evidence whose clarity and edge cut through rival claims.
- Active motifs: decisive proof `quranic:root_000732:B002/m01`; coercive authority `quranic:root_000732:B003/m01`; sharp tongue `quranic:root_000732:B004/m01`; sharp implement `quranic:root_000732:B006/m01`; manifest clarification `quranic:root_000170:B004/m01`; a thing’s own indication `quranic:root_001272:B014/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:45 سُلْطَٰنٍ / مُّبِينٍ; 23:47 قَالُ.
- Synthesis: Proof is not merely possessed; it operates. Clarity exposes, the tongue supplies an edge, and authority extends the instrument into the social field where a claim must answer the evidence.

### S7. P5: Diagnostic Presentation
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A hidden bodily condition becomes visible, presents residue and mortality signs, and calls for a physician’s prescription.
- Active motifs: visible sign of gestation `quranic:root_000531:B010/m01`; seeking a medical prescription `quranic:root_001654:B005/m01`; wound discharge `quranic:root_000333:B008/m01`; afterbirth residue `quranic:root_000333:B008/m02`; presence of harm `quranic:root_000333:B009/m01`; presence of death `quranic:root_000333:B009/m02`; internal disease `quranic:root_001642:B001/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:91 and 23:96 يَصِفُ; 23:93 and 23:95 تُرِيَ / نُّرِيَ; 23:98 يَحْضُرُ; 23:100 وَرَآئِ.
- Synthesis: Seeing, describing, and arrival form a clinical presentation. A hidden internal disease produces visible signs and residue; the condition “comes before” the observer and demands a prescribed response.

### S8. Whole-Surah: Embodied Prayer Rite
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A worshipper enters a dedicated place, faces a fixed direction, stands, counts praise on beads, and maintains the rite through voluntary repetition.
- Active motifs: prescribed prayer rite `quranic:root_000879:B003/m01`; dedicated prayer place `quranic:root_000879:B007/m01`; prayer direction `quranic:root_001198:B005/m01`; standing posture `quranic:root_001273:B002/m01`; praise-counting beads `quranic:root_000666:B006/m01`; continual observance `quranic:root_000342:B003/m01`; voluntary offering `quranic:root_000956:B005/m01`; submissive worship `quranic:root_000973:B003/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:2 and 23:9 صَلَاتِ / صَلَوَٰتِ / يُحَافِظُ; 23:16 قِيَٰمَةِ; 23:34 أَطَعْ; 23:47 عَٰبِدُونَ; 23:83 قَبْلُ; 23:91 سُبْحَٰنَ.
- Synthesis: The rite makes guarded prayer in 23:2 and 23:9 fully embodied: the worshipper takes a place, direction, posture, counting instrument, and repeated discipline. This supports the primary portrait of the believers by materializing humility and preservation as embodied orientation and recurrence rather than an unlocated inner attitude.

### S9. Whole-Surah: Perfumer’s Workbench
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A perfumer grinds aromatic materials on a stone, blends saffron and camphor into a compound, applies it, and leaves a recognizable scent.
- Active motifs: perfume-grinding stone `quranic:root_000879:B008/m01`; aromatic compound `quranic:root_000434:B010/m01`; anointing with the compound `quranic:root_000434:B010/m02`; fragrance substance `quranic:root_000961:B007/m01`; saffron ingredient `quranic:root_000974:B011/m01`; camphor fragrance `quranic:root_001307:B011/m01`; recognizable scent `quranic:root_001002:B004/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:2 and 23:9 صَلَاتِ / صَلَوَٰتِ; 23:14 خَلَقْ; 23:21 عِبْرَةً; 23:24 كَفَرُ; 23:51 طَّيِّبَٰتِ; 23:69 يَعْرِفُ.
- Synthesis: The workshop reframes the “good things” of 23:51 and recognition in 23:69: pleasantness is produced by measured preparation and travels outward as a perceptible trace. This usefully pressures rival claims to goodness, since what is truly good is prepared, applied, and made recognizable in its effects rather than merely asserted.

### S10. Whole-Surah: Hunter’s Snare and Captured Prey
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Hunters set out when prey comes within reach, plant snares, tighten a neck rope around the caught animal, verify its death, and distribute the game as meat.
- Active motifs: prey within reach `quranic:root_000421:B005/m01`; setting out to hunt `quranic:root_000745:B006/m01`; hunter’s snare `quranic:root_000791:B006/m01`; set trapping device `quranic:root_000879:B004/m01`; prey caught in a noose `quranic:root_001039:B011/m01`; neck rope `quranic:root_000783:B008/m01`; verifying the death of game `quranic:root_001454:B014/m01`; game meat as provision `quranic:root_001348:B003/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:2 and 23:9 صَلَاتِ / صَلَوَٰتِ; 23:14 عَلَقَةً / لَحْمًا; 23:15 مَيِّتُونَ; 23:18 سَّمَآءِ; 23:27 تُخَٰطِبْ; 23:33 يَشْرَبُ; 23:59 and 23:92 يُشْرِكُ.
- Synthesis: The hunt gives concrete force to the surah’s repeated movement from warning to inescapable seizure and death. Most sharply, the `ش ر ك` snare reframes the false partnership denied in 23:91-92 as the trapping device itself: the rival scheme that promises leverage becomes the mesh in which its prey is caught.

### S11. Whole-Surah: Stagnant Cistern and Wood-Eating Vermin
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Water collects in a broad basin and depression, becomes still and turbid under trampling, and supports proliferating vermin that consume the surrounding wood.
- Active motifs: broad collection basin `quranic:root_000016:B007/m01`; depression pool `quranic:root_000281:B003/m01`; trampled stagnant water `quranic:root_000932:B008/m01`; arrested water movement `quranic:root_001273:B016/m01`; wood-eating termite `quranic:root_000025:B010/m01`; water-beetle infestation `quranic:root_000248:B008/m01`; proliferating small ground creatures `quranic:root_000324:B004/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:13 جَعَلْ; 23:16 قِيَٰمَةِ; 23:17 طَرَآئِقَ; 23:18 أَرْضِ; 23:27 جَآءَ; 23:43 أَجَلَ; 23:79 تُحْشَرُ.
- Synthesis: This scene usefully pressures 23:18-20: measured water lodged in earth is provision only while it can be released into cultivation. Once holding becomes arrest, the pool turns turbid and feeds decay, materializing the surah’s distinction between ordered preservation and a community immobilized until corruption proliferates.

### S12. Whole-Surah: Backbiting Circle and Reputational Predation
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A speaker attacks an absent person before a listening circle; the insult is made audible, taken up, and spread until the target's honor is treated like prey.
- Active motifs: predatory attack on reputation `quranic:root_000669:B003/m01`; deliberately audible insult `quranic:root_000741:B006/m01`; mention of an absent person's fault `quranic:root_001117:B004/m01`; joking consumption of another's honor `quranic:root_001174:B007/m01`; fault-finding and backbiting `quranic:root_001600:B004/m01`; lending the ear to speech `quranic:root_000574:B004/m01`; reputation spread among listeners `quranic:root_000741:B005/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:8 رَٰعُونَ; 23:17 and 23:86 سَبْعَ / سَّبْعِ; 23:19 فَوَٰكِهُ; 23:24 and 23:78 سَمِعْ / سَّمْعَ; 23:92 غَيْبِ; 23:97 هَمَزَٰتِ.
- Synthesis: This usefully pressures the rejection of idle speech in 23:3 and the mockery recalled in 23:110. Verbal harm is not harmless residue: it recruits an audience, circulates a damaged reputation, and consumes the absent person socially.

### S13. Whole-Surah: Nightly Lunar-Mansion Watch
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: At twilight an observer follows the moon and named stars through recurrent stations and tracks until the lights sink toward the horizon.
- Active motifs: twilight after sunset `quranic:root_000803:B002/m01`; sun nearing its setting `quranic:root_000908:B006/m01`; moon entering a nightly mansion `quranic:root_000018:B008/m01`; three-star lunar station `quranic:root_001096:B006/m01`; encircling crown as lunar station `quranic:root_001315:B005/m01`; Aldebaran following the Pleiades `quranic:root_000458:B013/m01`; celestial track and stellar course `quranic:root_001177:B002/m01`; stars sinking from sight `quranic:root_000412:B003/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:2 خَٰشِعُونَ; 23:22 and 23:27-28 فُلْكِ / فُلْكَ; 23:27, 23:44, 23:53, 23:88, and 23:91 كُلٍّ / كُلَّ / كُلُّ / كُلِّ; 23:41, 23:64, 23:76, 23:91, and 23:110 أَخَذَتْ / أَخَذْ / ٱتَّخَذَ / ٱتَّخَذْ; 23:57 مُّشْفِقُونَ; 23:68 يَدَّبَّرُ; 23:76 يَتَضَرَّعُ; 23:109 and 23:118 ٱغْفِرْ.
- Synthesis: The watch supports 23:17 and 23:80 by materializing the paths above and the succession of night and day as recurrent, observable order. A heavenly route is not merely asserted; its stations, following relations, and disappearances can be tracked without the negligence denied in 23:17.

### S14. Whole-Surah: Noon Read from the Standing Shadow
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Morning opens, the day rises, and the shrinking shadow reaches a standing minimum by which the observer identifies midday and its heat.
- Active motifs: opening of morning `quranic:root_000839:B001/m01`; day rising and spreading `quranic:root_000546:B012/m01`; high or youthful day `quranic:root_001281:B013/m01`; contracting shadow `quranic:root_000908:B008/m01`; shadow arrested upright at noon `quranic:root_001036:B012/m01`; meridian standing point `quranic:root_001273:B017/m01`; balance of the day at its midpoint `quranic:root_001645:B004/m01`; heat of the midday interval `quranic:root_001578:B005/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:16 قِيَٰمَةِ; 23:25 and 23:38 رَجُلٌ; 23:40 يُصْبِحُ; 23:46 and 23:67 ٱسْتَكْبَرُوا / مُسْتَكْبِرِينَ; 23:67 تَهْجُرُ; 23:76 يَتَضَرَّعُ; 23:80 تَعْقِلُ; 23:102-103 مَوَٰزِينُ.
- Synthesis: The scene materializes the surah's time accounting in 23:112-114. Human duration can be estimated from a moving shadow, but the standing balance marks only one point in the interval; the final count belongs to the one who knows its whole course.

### S15. Whole-Surah: Milking Before and After Calving
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: As birth approaches, colostrum and milk gather in the udder; a reserve is left to draw the next flow, milk returns between milkings, and the kneeling camel is milked at dawn.
- Active motifs: nearness of calving `quranic:root_000493:B004/m01`; milk or colostrum entering the udder before birth `quranic:root_000480:B009/m01`; full and abundant udder `quranic:root_000810:B003/m01`; pleasant thick milk before delivery `quranic:root_001174:B004/m01`; reserved milk that calls forth the next flow `quranic:root_000478:B003/m01`; milk returning between milkings `quranic:root_001188:B006/m01`; dawn milk from a kneeling camel `quranic:root_000109:B007/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:14 تَبَارَكَ; 23:17 فَوْقَ; 23:19 فَوَٰكِهُ; 23:29 مُّبَارَكًا; 23:33 and 23:37 دُّنْيَا; 23:73 تَدْعُو; 23:78 تَشْكُرُ; 23:96 ٱدْفَعْ.
- Synthesis: This supports 23:21 by materializing drink from livestock as a timed reproductive and husbandry process. Provision is maintained through gestation, retained residue, recurrent letdown, and skilled milking rather than appearing as an undifferentiated store.

### S16. Whole-Surah: Calf Weaning Toggle
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A calf follows its mother and is first released to nurse freely; the herder can then place a spindle-like toggle on its tongue to block suckling.
- Active motifs: calf following its dam `quranic:root_000175:B007/m01`; release of the young animal with its mother for unrestricted nursing `quranic:root_000546:B014/m01`; tongue toggle that prevents nursing `quranic:root_001177:B006/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:22 and 23:27-28 فُلْكِ / فُلْكَ; 23:25 and 23:38 رَجُلٌ; 23:44 أَتْبَعْ; 23:71 ٱتَّبَعَ.
- Synthesis: The toggle usefully pressures 23:21 and the deprivation scene of 23:75-76. Access to nourishment can be opened by release or physically interrupted at the mouth, making provision and withholding two controlled states of one husbandry practice.

### S17. Whole-Surah: Milk Flow and Curdling
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Recurrent milk flows and drips, then thickens into curd; weak yield or a flow that does not persist marks failure of the process.
- Active motifs: repeated abundant milk flow `quranic:root_000563:B006/m01`; liquid dripping before thickening `quranic:root_001518:B003/m01`; milk curdling at the end of its flow `quranic:root_000067:B005/m01`; low milk yield `quranic:root_000497:B006/m01`; milk that disappears instead of continuing `quranic:root_001290:B006/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:13-14 نُطْفَةً / نُّطْفَةَ; 23:20 دُّهْنِ; 23:23, 23:32, 23:44-45, 23:51, and 23:69 أَرْسَلْ / رَسُولًا / رُسُلَ; 23:24, 23:68, 23:81, and 23:83 أَوَّلِينَ / أَوَّلُونَ; 23:90 كَٰذِبُونَ.
- Synthesis: This supports the livestock drink of 23:21 and the good foods of 23:51 by distinguishing sustained flow, useful transformation, and failed continuity. Provision must both arrive and hold long enough to become usable substance.

### S18. Whole-Surah: Dyer's Saturated Cloth
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A dyer saturates cloth with safflower color, works its raised nap, and produces a red or multicolored fabric whose appearance can misrepresent its condition.
- Active motifs: soaking cloth in dye `quranic:root_000722:B009/m01`; raised nap on dyed fabric `quranic:root_000621:B007/m01`; finished red cloth `quranic:root_001036:B013/m01`; multicolored fabric that "lies" by appearance `quranic:root_001290:B009/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:21 نُّسْقِي; 23:53 زُبُرًا; 23:80 تَعْقِلُ; 23:90 كَٰذِبُونَ.
- Synthesis: The workshop reframes the manufactured narrative of 23:33-38 and the lying claim of 23:90. Color can be driven into a surface until presentation appears intrinsic, so outward vividness cannot by itself certify truth.

### S19. Whole-Surah: Convalescent Meat Pot
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Meat is stripped from bone and cooked in a handled pot until its harshness is subdued; the broth feeds a wasted body, rebuilds flesh, and accompanies recovery.
- Active motifs: butcher-cook and cooking pot `quranic:root_001205:B007/m01`; heat cloth used to lower the pot `quranic:root_000248:B007/m01`; meat stripped from bone `quranic:root_001348:B009/m01`; food rebuilding bodily flesh `quranic:root_000156:B010/m01`; wasting disease that removes flesh and strength `quranic:root_000736:B008/m01`; cooking that subdues a substance's force `quranic:root_001454:B002/m01`; recovery from emaciating illness `quranic:root_000152:B003/m01`; convalescent improvement `quranic:root_001397:B012/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:12 سُلَٰلَةٍ; 23:13 جَعَلْ; 23:14 لَحْمًا; 23:15 مَيِّتُونَ; 23:18 قَدَرٍ; 23:50 ٱبْنَ; 23:81 مِثْلَ; surface anchor unavailable for ب ل ل.
- Synthesis: The pot supports 23:51 and the relief sought in 23:75 by making good food restorative work. It also reverses the flesh-over-bone sequence of 23:14: separated flesh becomes prepared nourishment that can build flesh back onto a depleted frame.

### S20. Whole-Surah: Morning Drinking Circle
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Companions gather for morning food and drink, take liquid in measured sips or breaths, and share rich fat or oil as condiment.
- Active motifs: morning food and drink `quranic:root_000839:B003/m01`; drinking a liquid `quranic:root_000783:B001/m01`; measured sip or drinking breath `quranic:root_001533:B006/m01`; drinking party at a shared source `quranic:root_000783:B003/m01`; habitual drinking companion `quranic:root_001485:B002/m01`; melted fat or oil used with food `quranic:root_000064:B006/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:27 أَهْلَ; 23:33 يَشْرَبُ / تَشْرَبُ; 23:40 يُصْبِحُ / نَٰدِمِينَ; 23:62 نَفْسًا; 23:103 أَنفُسَ.
- Synthesis: This supports 23:33 and 23:51 by locating eating and drinking in an ordinary reciprocal gathering. The elite objection that a messenger consumes food is pressured by a scene in which shared intake is social maintenance, not evidence against moral authority.

### S21. Whole-Surah: Pre-Dawn Sustenance Before a Fast
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Near the end of night, a fasting person takes a meal or drink that supplies bodily nourishment and preserves strength for the coming abstention.
- Active motifs: pre-dawn time `quranic:root_000682:B004/m01`; pre-dawn meal of food, milk, or meal-drink `quranic:root_000682:B005/m01`; nourishment required by an embodied eater `quranic:root_000682:B003/m01`; pre-dawn meal called success because it sustains the fast `quranic:root_001175:B006/m01`; food entering the body as sustenance `quranic:root_000560:B002/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:1 أَفْلَحَ; 23:72 رَّٰزِقِينَ; 23:89 تُسْحَرُ; 23:102 مُفْلِحُونَ; 23:117 يُفْلِحُ.
- Synthesis: The practice reframes success in 23:1 and 23:102 as strength maintained for disciplined restraint. Success is not an instant prize; it includes measured nourishment that enables a demanding observance to continue.

### S22. Whole-Surah: Sworn Formula and Right-Hand Bond
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A speaker invokes the divine name, opens with an affirming oath particle, swears, and binds the declaration through the right-hand relation.
- Active motifs: divine name used in oath and address `quranic:root_000047:B002/m01`; affirming particle that opens an oath `quranic:root_000074:B010/m01`; formal swearing and oath `quranic:root_000076:B007/m01`; right hand as oath and pledged bond `quranic:root_001698:B003/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:6 أَيْمَٰنُ; 23:14, 23:23-24, 23:28, 23:32, 23:38, 23:85, 23:87, 23:89, 23:91, and 23:116-117 ٱللَّه / إِلَٰه; 23:30, 23:45, 23:50, 23:58, 23:66, and 23:105 ءَايَٰت; surface anchor unavailable for ء ل ي.
- Synthesis: This supports the surah's testing of truthful and false speech, especially 23:90 and 23:117. A claim made under oath is not free-floating language; formula and pledged hand bind the speaker before the sovereign witness invoked by name.

### S23. Whole-Surah: Remarriage and the Stepchild Household
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A previously married woman with an older child receives suitors, is conveyed as a bride, and enters a new household in which the child acquires a step-parent relation.
- Active motifs: remarriage of a woman with an adult son `quranic:root_000109:B009/m01`; stepchild and caregiving step-parent `quranic:root_000532:B005/m01`; courtship messages to a widow or divorcee `quranic:root_000563:B009/m01`; bride conveyed to her husband `quranic:root_001583:B006/m01`; wedding entry and establishment of the union `quranic:root_000156:B006/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:14 and 23:29 تَبَارَكَ / مُّبَارَكًا; 23:23, 23:32, 23:44-45, 23:51, and 23:69 أَرْسَلْ / رَسُولًا / رُسُلَ; 23:49 يَهْتَدُ; 23:50 and 23:55 ٱبْنَ / بَنِينَ.
- Synthesis: The scene materializes the guarded sexual field of 23:5-7 as a transition between recognized social states. A lawful union reassigns household roles and obligations, including care for dependents carried from an earlier marriage.

### S24. Whole-Surah: Hidden-Hand Odd-or-Even Game
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: One player conceals walnuts in a hand, another calls odd or even, and the hand opens to disclose the exact count.
- Active motifs: game of producing what is hidden in the hand `quranic:root_000400:B010/m01`; "khassa" call for an odd walnut count `quranic:root_000408:B003/m01`; "zaka" call for an even count `quranic:root_000637:B005/m01`; odd singleton opposed to a pair `quranic:root_001621:B001/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:4 زَّكَوٰةِ; 23:20 تَخْرُجُ; 23:35 مُّخْرَجُونَ; 23:44 تَتْرَا; 23:72 خَرْجًا / خَرَاجُ; 23:107-108 أَخْرِجْ / ٱخْسَـُٔ.
- Synthesis: The game usefully pressures 23:112-115, where a guessed duration meets an exact count and purposeless play is denied. Hidden quantity permits speculation only until disclosure; opening the hand ends approximation.

### S25. Whole-Surah: Maysir Arrow Draw
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Lot arrows are gathered in a leather container, distinguished by rank, and drawn so that one participant receives the losing lot while another obtains the higher share.
- Active motifs: leather receptacle holding maysir arrows `quranic:root_000532:B010/m01`; losing lot opposed to the winning arrow `quranic:root_000458:B019/m01`; fifth maysir arrow `quranic:root_001533:B016/m01`; highest-ranked lot arrow `quranic:root_001042:B009/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:46 عَالِينَ; 23:62 نَفْسًا; 23:68 يَدَّبَّرُ; 23:91-92 عَلَا / تَعَٰلَىٰ; 23:103 أَنفُسَ; 23:116 تَعَٰلَى.
- Synthesis: The draw reframes success by contrast. The flourishing of 23:1 and the weighted outcome of 23:102 are not chance allotments from a bag; rank follows accountable action rather than a winning arrow.

### S26. Whole-Surah: Arafat Station and Pilgrim's Return
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A pilgrim reaches the sacred locality, stands at Arafat, uses a known lodging or station, and completes a return associated with pilgrimage.
- Active motifs: standing at Arafat on its appointed day `quranic:root_001002:B007/m01`; sacred locality or valley `quranic:root_000666:B008/m01`; familiar station to which travelers return `quranic:root_001055:B005/m01`; pilgrim's return and destination `quranic:root_001058:B002/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:8 عَهْدِ; 23:69 يَعْرِفُ; 23:91 سُبْحَٰنَ; 23:107 عُدْ.
- Synthesis: The rite materializes directed return in 23:115 as an itinerary of approach, standing, and coming back from a recognized station. Ritual return rehearses orientation; the surah's final return makes that orientation universal rather than optional.

### S27. Whole-Surah: Burial on the Right Side
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: The dead person is wrapped or enclosed, laid on the right side, and hidden within the grave.
- Active motifs: shrouding and grave enclosure `quranic:root_000266:B009/m01`; burial as hiding in the grave `quranic:root_001117:B009/m01`; laying the dead on the right side `quranic:root_001698:B007/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:6 أَيْمَٰنُ; 23:19 جَنَّٰتٍ; 23:25 and 23:70 جِنَّةٌ; 23:92 غَيْبِ.
- Synthesis: The rite materializes the transition from death in 23:15 to the blocked request in 23:99-100. Concealment is performed on the body itself, so the separating interval begins from a concrete, socially completed placement.

### S28. Whole-Surah: Ember-Baked Bread and Basket
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Fire is tended to roast or bake a loaf in embers, and the finished bread is placed in a covered basket.
- Active motifs: roasting and baking in fire or hot ash `quranic:root_001122:B001/m01`; baked loaf `quranic:root_001122:B001/m02`; lidded bread basket `quranic:root_000736:B011/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:12 سُلَٰلَةٍ; 23:78 أَفْـِٔدَةَ.
- Synthesis: Domestic heat supports the good food of 23:51 while contrasting with the face-burning fire of 23:104. The same elemental force yields provision when bounded by skilled work and injury when it becomes punitive exposure.

### S29. Whole-Surah: Invited Guest Banquet
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A host calls companions to a prepared meal, receives the arriving guest, and assigns food, lodging, and an edible share.
- Active motifs: invitation to food `quranic:root_000478:B001/m01`; feast prepared for invited companions `quranic:root_000885:B010/m01`; provisions and lodging prepared for a guest `quranic:root_001492:B005/m01`; edible allotment or ration `quranic:root_000043:B003/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:18, 23:24, and 23:29 أَنزَلْ / أَنزَلَ / أَنزِلْ; 23:19-21, 23:33, and 23:51 تَأْكُلُ / ءَاكِلِينَ / يَأْكُلُ / كُلُ; 23:27 ٱصْنَعِ; 23:73 and 23:117 تَدْعُو / يَدْعُ.
- Synthesis: The banquet supports 23:51 and reframes the repeated reception of messengers as a hospitality test. A call creates an obligation to receive and provision the arrival; rejection therefore withholds more than assent, severing the social duties activated by the invitation.

### S30. Whole-Surah: Tattooer's Repeated Lines
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Skin is punctured, dark pigment made from wick or fat soot is applied, and faded lines are repeatedly darkened into a durable bodily mark.
- Active motifs: repeated tattoo lines and renewed darkening `quranic:root_000544:B009/m01`; skin puncture followed by soot pigment `quranic:root_001564:B008/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:60 رَٰجِعُونَ; 23:99 ٱرْجِعُ; 23:104 نَّارُ; 23:115 تُرْجَعُ.
- Synthesis: The craft supports the truthful record of 23:62 by materializing persistence as a trace fixed into the body. Repetition does not merely recall a mark; it renews its visibility, pressing the surah's concern with what remains retrievable after speech and action pass.

### S31. Whole-Surah: Dream Interpretation
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A sleeper sees a dream, and an interpreter moves from its visible form through its aspects to an intelligible meaning or lesson.
- Active motifs: dream seen during sleep `quranic:root_000531:B003/m01`; interpretation that carries a dream from appearance to meaning `quranic:root_000974:B002/m01`; exemplum read as a lesson or sign `quranic:root_001397:B011/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:21 عِبْرَةً; 23:24, 23:33-34, 23:47, and 23:81 مِّثْلُ / مِّثْلَ / مِثْلِ; 23:93 and 23:95 تُرِيَ / نُّرِيَ.
- Synthesis: The practice supports the demand to ponder speech in 23:68 and pressures the dismissal of inherited material as mere tales in 23:83. An image may require disciplined transfer from appearance to significance rather than either credulous repetition or immediate rejection.

### S32. Whole-Surah: Separated Flock under Predation
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A small flock breaks from the larger group, becomes exposed, and is taken as prey by wolves or other predators.
- Active motifs: small flock separated or lost from the group `quranic:root_001148:B005/m01`; livestock predator `quranic:root_000669:B002/m01`; wolf named by its turning behavior `quranic:root_001248:B013/m01`; wolf-hyena predator `quranic:root_000741:B010/m01`; sheep isolated or fattened as prey `quranic:root_000043:B007/m01`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:17 and 23:86 سَبْعَ / سَّبْعِ; 23:19-21, 23:33, and 23:51 تَأْكُلُ / ءَاكِلِينَ / يَأْكُلُ / كُلُ; 23:24 and 23:78 سَمِعْ / سَّمْعَ; 23:60 and 23:63 قُلُوبُ; 23:109 فَرِيقٌ.
- Synthesis: The scene reframes the factional break in 23:52-53. Division is not only conceptual disagreement; it removes the safety of coordinated movement and turns the separated group into available prey.

### S33. Whole-Surah: Postpartum Fenugreek Decoction
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Fenugreek is boiled until it rises, strained, mixed with dates, and given as a drink to a postpartum woman.
- Active motifs: boiling fenugreek `quranic:root_001185:B006/m01`; straining the decoction `quranic:root_001185:B006/m02`; adding dates `quranic:root_001185:B006/m03`; postpartum restorative drink `quranic:root_001185:B006/m04`.
- Ayah anchors: 23:27 فَارَ.
- Synthesis: The preparation supports the postpartum affliction activated around 23:75-76 by adding a concrete practice of restorative care. Relief is materialized as timed boiling, filtering, enrichment, and intake rather than as an unworked reversal of pain.

## Cross-Pericope Channels

### X1. Flow Regime Determines Outcome
- Pericopes: P1, P2, P3, and P4; whole-surah lexical scene S11.
- Bridge: repeated hydraulic scene signature joined by a causal state sequence and contrast.
- Shared invariant: Liquid force yields provision, destruction, distress, or decay according to how it is measured, contained, routed, pressured, and released.
- Canonical placements: P1 Parent 3, Subchannels A-B, “Descent, Storage, and Withdrawal” and “Irrigation and Cultivated Emergence”; P2 Parent 6, “Catastrophe as Hydraulic Conversion”; P3 Parent 12, “Water-Fed Interior”; P4 Parent 16, Subchannel A, “Deep-Water Pressure”; whole-surah S11, “Stagnant Cistern and Wood-Eating Vermin”.
- Synthesis: Metered descent and routed irrigation produce yield in P1; failed containment converts the same force into engulfment and residue in P2; P3 transfers the catchment signature into the interior; P4 intensifies it as pressure against a constrained margin; S11 supplies the terminal contrast of water arrested into stagnation. Across these placements, changes in flow state govern the transition from life-giving provision to engulfment, interior distress, threshold pressure, and decay.

### X2. Guarded Frontier Becomes Final Partition
- Pericopes: P1, P4, and P5.
- Bridge: repeated threshold scene signature with role progression and terminal reversal.
- Shared invariant: Protected order depends on an authorized boundary that determines who may cross, in which direction, and at what time.
- Canonical placements: P1 Parent 1, Subchannel B, “Bodily Frontier and Controlled Passage”; P4 Parent 16, Subchannel B, “Outlet, Gate, and Speechless Exclusion”; P5 Parent 22, Subchannel B, “Separating Interval and Suspended Launch”.
- Synthesis: In P1 the ethical subject guards a frontier against unauthorized passage; in P4 authority controls the opening and excludes the party at the gate; in P5 the former traveler stands behind an irreversible partition awaiting release. The role progresses from custodian to gate-governed subject, while controlled passage reverses into barred return.

### X3. Claim Becomes Record and Verdict
- Pericopes: P2, P3, P4, and P5.
- Bridge: causal sequence and role progression from speaker to registrar, archive, and tribunal.
- Shared invariant: Speech becomes accountable when circulation leaves a recoverable trace that can be registered, tested against a right-bearing record, and bounded by judgment.
- Canonical placements: P2 Parent 8, Subchannel B, “Manufactured Public Narrative”; P3 Parent 11, Subchannel A, “Capacity-Calibrated Record”; P4 Parent 17, Subchannel B, “Rows, Title Deeds, and Landmarks”; P5 Parent 25, “Speech Tribunal”.
- Synthesis: P2 supplies the circulating manufactured claim; P3 places accountable bearers and burdens into a calibrated register; P4 preserves marks by which legend can be distinguished from valid title; P5 tests attribution and closes the reply channel by verdict. The claim’s causal progression through durable evidence turns speech into an object of accountability whose final limit is judgment.

### X4. Measured Origination Ends in Return
- Pericopes: P1, P2, P4, and P5.
- Bridge: causal sequence and role progression from formed body to cohort, dispersed material, reassembled creature, and intended return.
- Shared invariant: Creation remains ordered across scale and time because measured origination carries its products toward reassembly and a purposive endpoint.
- Canonical placements: P1 Parent 2, “Staged Embodiment”; P2 Parent 7, Subchannel A, “Bound Generation Units”; P4 Parent 19, “Resurrection as Agricultural Recovery”; P5 Parent 27, Subchannel B, “Calculation Against Purposeless Play”.
- Synthesis: P1 measures and assembles one body; P2 repeats origination at the scale of bounded generations; P4 recasts dispersed matter as seed, residue, and dormant structure gathered into renewed form; P5 identifies return as the endpoint that prevents creation from being purposeless play. The making operation advances through one role sequence in which form, lineage, dispersed matter, and returned creature occupy successive stages.
